facts.text: Combat was the pack-in game for the Atari 2600 at launch in 1977, offering 27 game variations in a single cartridge
Pitfall! on the Atari 2600 sold over 4 million copies and was one of the first true action-adventure games
E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial cartridges were famously buried in a New Mexico landfill in 1983
Crash Bandicoot used a streaming technique to load levels without visible load screens
Tomb Raider's Lara Croft was originally conceived as a male archaeologist before the team switched to a female lead
Alien vs. Predator for the Jaguar was praised as one of the best first-person shooters of 1994
The Atari 2600 launched in 1977 at $199, which is equivalent to over $900 in today's money, making it a significant household investment
Mega Man 2 was turned down by Capcom, so the team built it on personal time — it became the series' best-selling game
The Konami Code debuted in Gradius on NES, granting players full power-ups — it became the most famous cheat code in gaming
EarthBound on SNES had aggressive anti-piracy code that crashed the game near the final boss if piracy was detected
Star Fox used the Super FX chip — a custom graphics co-processor built into the cartridge — to render 3D polygons

Secret of Mana's ring-based menu system could be opened mid-action

Sonic & Knuckles used 'lock-on technology' to physically combine with Sonic 2 or 3 cartridges for expanded content

GoldenEye 007 was developed by a team with almost no prior game development experience

Shenmue was the most expensive video game ever made at the time of its 1999 release

Shadow of the Colossus featured only 16 enemies across its entire world, each one a full environmental puzzle

Panzer Dragoon Saga is one of the rarest Saturn games, with only 6,000 copies printed in North America

Radiant Silvergun for Saturn is considered one of the greatest shoot-em-ups ever made and commands very high collector prices
Dragon Force on Saturn featured battles with up to 100 soldiers fighting simultaneously on screen
Fatal Fury introduced a two-plane fighting system where characters could dodge between a foreground and background

Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow introduced the soul system, letting players absorb enemy abilities as power-ups

Road Rash on 3DO featured full-motion video cutscenes and was considered a showcase title for the system

Alex Kidd in Miracle World was built into many Master System consoles as a pack-in game

Snatcher, Hideo Kojima's cyberpunk visual novel, was released on Sega CD and is now extremely rare and valuable

Final Fantasy I through VI were all remade exclusively for the WonderSwan Color in Japan
SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters Clash was a card strategy game for the NGPC blending characters from both companies
Wario Land was considered the Virtual Boy's strongest title
New Super Mario Bros. was the first new 2D Mario platformer in over a decade when it launched on DS in 2006

Brain Age on DS became a surprise phenomenon, attracting an older audience and selling over 19 million copies worldwide

Commando was one of the most praised arcade ports on the Atari 7800 for its faithful recreation of the cabinet

Splatoon debuted on the Wii U in 2015, marking Nintendo's first successful new major IP in many years
Super Smash Bros. for Wii U supported 8-player simultaneous battles on large stages

Castlevania II: Simon's Quest added a day/night cycle and towns, unlike the original's linear structure

Lufia II featured a 99-floor randomly generated dungeon — one of the earliest roguelike elements on SNES
